note: 10 stage-1 concept abstracts (seeded draw, one or two per shelf), each claim checked by eye against the page IMAGE and the stored page text (job embed-next-6173, 2026-10-07). 'image' = the claim was read on the scan itself; 'text' = only supported by the stored translation/notes; 'gloss' = not on the page.

pages.title: Lotus Sutra (Sixi Tripitaka ed.)

claims.claim: belief in a permanent self is a fundamental error that prevents spiritual progress
claims.why: the page says only 'do not preach this sutra to those who hold the view of self' (計我見者 莫說此經); 'fundamental error … prevents progress' is the translator's footnote

claims.claim: those deeply attached to sensory desires
claims.why: 凡夫淺識 深著五欲

claims.claim: those who reject the teaching face severe moral consequences
claims.why: 毀謗此經 則斷一切世間佛種 … 此人罪報

pages.verdict: faithful except one claim taken from a translator's note

pages.title: The Great Meaning of the Five Elements

claims.claim: existence vs non-existence is defined by vital energy rather than physical form
claims.why: the page ties 'existence' to the living form (生則形存為有) and non-existence to qi dispersing at death (死則氣散為無); 'rather than physical form' inverts it

claims.claim: spirits lack a tangible body but have a moral quality that lets them affect human affairs
claims.why: 鬼神雖無形質 可見而有善惡 可求故能為抑

claims.claim: their power is real without physical substance
claims.why: same passage

claims.claim: descending into others' darkness/suffering to share their transformation
claims.why: uns einer zum andern in die Hölle versencken, und werden was unser Bruder ist

claims.claim: described as a difficult birth
claims.why: die schwereste Geburt in allen unsern Tagen

claims.claim: the divine creative command must intervene to cleanse the primordial material of the soul
claims.why: the Fiat enters and is cast out (das Fiat eingieng … warf sie das Fiat aus); 'cleanse the primordial material' is not on the page

claims.claim: identifying with others' struggles, one shares in their redemption
claims.why: so empfahen wir an dieser holdseligen Geburt gleiche Theil

pages.title: Greek texts on mathematics, astronomy and geography (CUL Gg.2.33)

claims.claim: the product of two sexagesimal parts is of an order equal to the sum of the orders
claims.why: πρῶτα / τρίτα / τέταρτα ἑξηκοστὰ … πολλαπλασιασθῇ legible in the hand; the worked progression is the page's subject

claims.claim: governed by proportions that hold regardless of the values used
claims.why: the page cites the proportion theorem of Elements II; 'regardless of the values' is a generalisation

claims.claim: chemistry is a tool for medicine but should not be its foundation
claims.why: Sylvius/Tachenius rejected for making medicine 'ein blosser Zweig' of chemistry; 'mit gehöriger Einschränkung'

claims.claim: chemistry is essential to the crafts that transform substances for aesthetic value
claims.why: §. 4 Einfluß der Chemie auf die … Handwerkskünste … Färbekünste; painting, ultramarine on the facing page

claims.claim: geometrical abstractions are not mere phantoms of the mind but serve to understand the passage from the unmanifest to the physical
claims.why: argues against 'simply a phantom of the mind'; 'Esoteric application to the idea of the pregenesis, and the genesis of Kosmos'

claims.claim: a progression from the indivisible point to the solid
claims.why: from the mathematical indivisible point to solid figures

claims.claim: the goddesses of the diagrams reside in the body's energy centres
claims.why: सुषुम्नामध्यसंस्थेषु षडाधाराम्बुजेषु ताः । तिष्ठन्ति प्राणिनां देव्यः

claims.claim: realised by inner understanding and outer ritual
claims.why: ज्ञानपूजिताः … बहिश्च मण्डले पूजा

claims.claim: worship at bodily sites and altars brings wisdom and protection from harm
claims.why: तया सर्वज्ञतासिद्धिः; वेदिका, गन्धपुष्पधूप and अमङ्गलानि न सम्भवन्ति in the commentary

pages.title: Trithemius in Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1531 ed.)

claims.claim: patient endurance of persecution is a sign of grace and leads to reward
claims.why: certum est signum, quod in Dei gratia saluandus perseuerat; accipiet coronam uitae

claims.claim: prosperity is no sign of approval; the wicked flourish
claims.why: Quare impij uiuunt … confortati diuitijs … manifestum damnationis est signum

pages.title: De Visser, The Dragon in China and Japan

claims.claim: a pond's unchanging level read as a sign of the world's state; a sudden drop signals disaster
claims.why: the Sacred Pond of Higo; the diviners' 'calamity of drought'; 840 proclamation

claims.claim: a legend about a ruler's body explains a custom and a word
claims.why: Ōjin's dragon tail, the suso skirt, biryū → birō

claims.claim: writing and customs can arise independently in distant nations rather than by migration
claims.why: quid obest quin aliquae gentes … invenerint eadem … cum aliis gentibus maxime dissitis

claims.claim: a sect arising in one region need not spread at once; long independent laws and rites
claims.why: Foe born 1308 BC, doctrines brought to China ~900 years later; legibus ritibusque non peregrinis, at suis

summary.finding: The input text includes the translator's notes, so an abstract can carry the translator's gloss as if it were the page's claim (#0). Two pages were two-page spreads; the abstract followed the page's own translation, not the facing page.
